instruction: Use ANSYS Fluent via the Command Line Interface (CLI) to complete a 3D laminar pipe-flow analysis. Physical problem: Steady laminar flow of water through a straight circular pipe. Coordinate system and geometry: - Use a 3D model. - Use SI units in Fluent. - The pipe axis is along the global X direction. - The pipe length is 100 mm, equivalent to 0.100 m. - The pipe diameter is 4 mm, equivalent to 0.004 m. - The pipe radius is 0.002 m. - The circular cross-section is centered on the X axis: - Cross-section center: Y = 0 m, Z = 0 m - Radius: 0.002 m - The pipe domain should extend from: - X = 0 m at the inlet - X = 0.100 m at the outlet Boundary zone names: - Name the inlet boundary: inlet - Name the outlet boundary: outlet - Name the pipe wall boundary: wall Model parameters: - Fluid: water - Use constant material properties: - Density: 998.2 kg/m³ - Dynamic viscosity: 0.001003 Pa·s - Mesh: - Use a structured hexahedral or swept mesh. - Include 3 boundary-layer layers near the pipe wall. - Use sufficient axial and radial resolution to resolve the laminar velocity profile. Boundary conditions: - Inlet: - Velocity inlet - Mean inlet velocity = 0.1 m/s in the positive X direction - Outlet: - Pressure outlet - Gauge pressure = 0 Pa - Pipe wall: - Stationary no-slip wall Solver setup: - Solver type: pressure-based - Time setting: steady - Flow model: laminar - Pressure-velocity coupling: SIMPLE - Spatial discretization: second-order schemes where applicable - Initialize the solution and iterate until convergence. Save requirements: - Use C:\Users\user\Desktop as the working directory. - Save the Fluent case file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\pipe_laminar.cas - Save the Fluent data file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\pipe_laminar.dat [Software] To start ANSYS Workbench, run `C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v261\fluent\ntbin\win64\fluent.exe -g` (version/path may differ on your machine).

instruction: Use ANSYS Mechanical APDL to build and solve a 3D transient thermal conduction model. Physical problem: One-dimensional transient heat conduction in a semi-infinite-like steel block. Coordinate system and geometry: - Use the global Cartesian coordinate system. - Heat conduction is along the X direction. - The long direction of the block is X. - The block occupies: - 0 ≤ X ≤ 50 mm - 0 ≤ Y ≤ 20 mm - 0 ≤ Z ≤ 20 mm - The left end face is the face at X = 0. - The other end face is the face at X = 50 mm. - The model should behave as a one-dimensional conduction problem along X. Model parameters: - Block size: 50 mm × 20 mm × 20 mm - Material: steel - Use a unit-consistent mm-s-J-kg-°C system: - Thermal conductivity: 0.05 W/(mm·°C), equivalent to 50 W/(m·K) - Specific heat: 460 J/(kg·°C) - Density: 7.85e-6 kg/mm³, equivalent to 7850 kg/m³ - Element type: SOLID70 - Mesh: global element size 2 mm - The mesh should contain nodes at X = 4 mm and X = 6 mm. A regular 2 mm mesh along X satisfies this requirement. Boundary and initial conditions: - Initial temperature of the whole model: 20 °C - Left end face at X = 0: prescribed temperature 100 °C - All other external surfaces, including X = 50 mm, Y = 0, Y = 20 mm, Z = 0, and Z = 20 mm, are adiabatic. Analysis type: - Transient thermal analysis - Total analysis time: 10 s - Initial time step: 0.1 s - Save the final result at t = 10 s. Save requirements: - Use C:\Users\user\Desktop as the ANSYS working directory. - Save the database file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\apdl_transient_thermal.db - Save the thermal result file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\apdl_transient_thermal.rth. instruction: Use ANSYS Mechanical APDL to build and solve a 2D axisymmetric structural model of a thick-walled cylinder under internal pressure. Physical problem: Axisymmetric thick-walled cylinder under internal pressure. Coordinate system and geometry: - Use the global Cartesian coordinate system for the axisymmetric cross-section. - X is the radial direction. - Y is the axial direction. - The cylinder has an inner diameter of 50 mm and an outer diameter of 100 mm. - Therefore, model the radial domain from X = 25 mm to X = 50 mm. - The axial thickness is 10 mm. - Model the rectangular axisymmetric cross-section: - 25 ≤ X ≤ 50 mm - 0 ≤ Y ≤ 10 mm - Do not model or constrain a symmetry axis at X = 0, because the cylinder has a central hole and the axis is outside the modeled annular cross-section. Model parameters: - Material: linear elastic steel - Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa - Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3 - Element type: PLANE183 with axisymmetric option enabled - Mesh: global element size 5 mm Boundary conditions and load: - Inner cylindrical surface at X = 25 mm: apply an internal pressure of 10 MPa acting on the cylinder wall. - Outer cylindrical surface at X = 50 mm: free surface. - Axial faces: - At Y = 0 mm: constrain axial displacement UY = 0. - At Y = 10 mm: constrain axial displacement UY = 0. - Do not constrain radial displacement UX on the inner or outer cylindrical surfaces. Analysis type: - Static structural analysis. Save requirements: - Use C:\Users\user\Desktop as the ANSYS working directory. - Save the database file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\apdl_cylinder.db - Save the structural result file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\apdl_cylinder.rst Run the solver to completion and ensure a result file is generated.

instruction: Use ANSYS Mechanical APDL to build and solve a coupled thermal-structural analysis model. Physical problem: A straight steel bar is axially restrained and subjected to a uniform temperature increase. Coordinate system and geometry: - Use the global Cartesian coordinate system. - The bar length is along the X direction. - The bar occupies: - 0 ≤ X ≤ 100 mm - 0 ≤ Y ≤ 10 mm - 0 ≤ Z ≤ 10 mm - The left end face is X = 0. - The right end face is X = 100 mm. Model parameters: - Block size: 100 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm - Material: linear elastic steel with thermal expansion properties: - Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa - Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3 - Coefficient of thermal expansion α = 1.5e-5 /°C - Element type: SOLID185 - Mesh: global element size 5 mm Thermal condition: - Set the reference temperature for thermal strain to 20 °C. - Apply a uniform body temperature of 100 °C to the entire bar. Structural boundary conditions: - Restrain axial expansion by applying UX = 0 on both end faces: - X = 0 - X = 100 mm - Add only the minimum additional constraints required to prevent rigid-body motion in 3D space. For a solid model, this requires fixing translational degrees of freedom at strategically selected nodes on the same end face, for example: - At node (0, 0, 0): fix UY = 0 and UZ = 0. - At node (0, 10, 0): fix UZ = 0. - Do not fully constrain the lateral surfaces. Analysis type: - Static structural analysis with thermal strain. - The temperature field is applied as a uniform body load for thermal strain calculation. Save requirements: - Use C:\Users\user\Desktop as the ANSYS working directory. - Save the database file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\apdl_thermal_stress.db - Save the structural result file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\apdl_thermal_stress.rst Run the solver to completion and ensure a result file is generated.
